subject: [RFC PATCH v3 0/8] batch lookups in follow_page_mask()

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledges that there is an issue with FOLL_WRITE folios not setting their dirty bits after writing, but is unsure how to improve the situation without extensive filesystem changes.
reviews.raw_body:
That still leaves the question on what to do with
code paths that rely on get_user_pages(FOLL_WRITE)
to set the dirty bit on pages, and then do not set
the dirty bit themselves after they write the page.

Would it be better to move the dirty bit setting
till after the write (to the page) has happened,
even if that code does not queue up a filesystem
write?

Does unpin_user_pages_dirty_lock() need to call
Folio_set_checked() ?

You've made it pretty clear what is wrong, but
I'm confused as to how we could improve the situation,
at least without waiting for extensive filesystem
changes first.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-08-24.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of follow_page_mask() by allowing it to batch lookups and reduce lock contention. The current implementation walks the page tables one page at a time, even when contiguous pages are requested. This series changes follow_page_mask() to return a count and an array of pages, instead of a single struct page, enabling more efficient handling of large folios. Patches 1-4 prepare for this change by refactoring and splitting existing functions. Patch 5 optimizes huge page paths, patch 6 simplifies the handling of subpages, and patches 7 and 8 implement batched lookups and refcount batching, respectively. The series includes benchmark results showing a significant performance improvement.

reviews.author: Rik van Riel
reviews.summary: Raised a question about the code path and asked if there is another performance-critical path that goes through get_user_pages().

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Clarified that the main user of iov_iter_extract_bvecs is actually another caller, and pointed out a performance issue with the current implementation.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Aug 25, 2026 at 09:37:09AM -0400, Rik van Riel wrote:
> > And what many including the most performance critical callers want
> > instead is really a single bio_vec. Maybe we can go the extra step
> > for
> > that, as it would reduce the number of calls into gup significantly.
> > 
> Which code are you referring to here?
> 
> blk_rq_map_user() seems to end up calling pin_user_pages_fast(),
> via iov_iter_extract_user_pages, and it directly fills in the
> bio_vec's pages array.
> 
> Is there another performance critical path that goes
> through the slower get_user_pages() path?

The other callers of iov_iter_extract_bvecs matter more, but this is
the main user.

And iov_iter_extract_bvecs right now is very inefficient when used
on larger folios, as each call to iov_iter_extract_bvecs and thus
iov_iter_extract_pages and iov_iter_extract_user_pages can only
fill in up to 256 pages.  On x86 that is a single PMD mapped
folio.  Passing down the bio_vec array means that for PMD-mapped
ranges we reduce the calls into pin_user_pages_fast by a factor
of 256.

2026-08-25.patch_summary: Batch lookups in follow_page_mask() to improve performance of large folios.
